title: Show HN: Toli – Let Claude Code on one computer work with Codex on another
excerpt: toli — the telephone for AI agents ☎️ toli (टोली, "toh-lee") is Hindi for a band of people working together. With toli, your AI agents can work together no matter which harness they run in (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, … or one you built yourself) or where they run, and with any agent that already speaks A2A. They can collaborate on one machine or across the internet with a teammate's agents, handing off tasks, asking each other questions and sending back results over the open A2A protocol. It's not just for coding agents. Any agent with an MCP client can join, so a personal assistant can check with your coding agent before it answers you: How it works You run one toli daemon. Eac
more: h of your agents gets a name and a token there, which it uses to reach toli over MCP, on localhost. Each agent has peers : the other agents it's allowed to work with, on your daemon or someone else's. Only you can add peers, never the agent. Pairing exchanges a token in each direction. Agents and their peers send each other tasks over A2A. They can delegate work, ask questions and send back results. When a task arrives, toli wakes your agent and notifies it. You can watch and manage all their tasks (a TUI), or with the CLI. Install macOS or Linux: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arjunvlama/toli/main/install.sh Homebrew: brew install arjunvlama/tap/toli Windows (PowerShell): irm https: raw.githubusercontent.com arjunvlama main install.ps1 With Go: go install github.com/arjunvlama/toli/cmd/toli@latest Then start the daemon in the background: toli daemon install toli daemon status toli daemon stop start uninstall manage it. Agents on the same machine A two-minute quickstart. 1. Add the agents, and connect them to toli. Run this in the folder where you start each agent: where you type claude codex , or the folder you opened in your editor (its built-in terminal starts there). --connect names the agent's harness ( all harnesses ), and peers see the description when deciding what to send it. /src/web-ui toli agent add alice --description Owns the web UI --connect claude-code /src/api toli agent add bob --description Owns the API --connect codex Each prints what it did: ✓ Added agent 'alice'. card_url  http://127.0.0.1:7422/a2a/alice/.well-known/agent-card.json ✓ Connected Claude Code to agent 'alice' in ~/src/web-ui (~/.claude.json, .claude/settings.local.json). title: Show HN: Mnemolith – AI coding memory that goes stale when your code changes
excerpt: Mnemolith Shared memory for AI coding tools that stays true to your code. Mnemolith (NEE-mo-lith): "memory stone." What your AI learns, carved where every tool can read it. ( Why the name Formerly Aether Cache. If you installed aether-cache , see Moving from Aether Cache : your memories come with you. Website PyPI Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI tools each forget your project between sessions, and when they do remember things, nothing checks whether those memories are still correct. Mnemolith gives every tool one shared, local memory, and keeps it honest: Memories go stale when the code changes. Each memory is linked to the files it's about, with a snapshot of their git content hash. When
more: docker-compose.yml changes, the memory about it is retired automatically instead of being fed to your AI forever. Contradictions get replaced, not hoarded. "We migrated to MySQL" retires "we use Postgres" instead of sitting next to it and confusing the model. Near-identical repeats are merged. Every memory can explain itself. Which tool and session saved it, which file versions it was based on, and every change since: created, seen again, went stale, confirmed, replaced. It works with the files you already use. Current memories sync into a managed section of AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md , so they're committed, reviewed in PRs, and visible to teammates who don't run Mnemolith. It runs entirely on your machine, on top of a database engine I wrote from scratch. Not a Redis clone Mnemolith started as a from-scratch rebuild of Redis in Java, then kept going. Every layer here is written from scratch, and each one does something the layer beneath it can't: Layer What it adds MCP server Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP tool share one memory Git awareness Memories retire themselves when the code they describe changes Memory layer Status, provenance, full history, duplicate merging, and conflict review, inside the engine HNSW vector index Semantic search: 99.4% recall at 0.84 ms on 100K vectors, 22× faster than exact search Redis-compatible engine RESP protocol, 50+ commands, replication, transactions, and crash-safe persistence (0 acknowledged writes lost across 1,039,890 writes and 8 kill -9 crashes), at 88–93% of real Redis's throughput The bottom layer alone is a working Redis: redis-cli redis-benchmark , and redis-py talk to it unchanged.
